means: Literal danbooru FILE METADATA, not a description: absurdly high resolution, applied automatically on the site to uploads at or above roughly 3200px on a side. It says nothing about content - it describes the file the image arrived in.
does: Because it was auto-applied, the model learned it as a correlate of what very large scans and illustrations look like: dense fine detail, crisp hair strands, fully rendered backgrounds. So it buys DETAIL DENSITY. It does NOT and cannot change your output resolution - that is a graph parameter (EmptyLatentImage, 1344x768 here), not a prompt tag. Expecting absurdres to produce a bigger image is the classic misreading of this tag, and it is the clearest example in the set of danbooru grammar being metadata rather than description.
reach_for_it: on the anime path as part of the standard block, and especially on wide establishing shots where you want the background fully rendered rather than suggested
used_in: the tail of every prompt in movies/derby-ep1.json and derby-qwen.json
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
